title: Invertibility of the single-module direct-image unit for an acyclic module
statement: Choose shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let f:X→S be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], with injective resolutions in X.Modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let M be an O_X-module. If every positive ordinary right-derived direct image R^qf_*M is zero [def-pc-derived-direct-image], then the explicit single-complex comparison followed by the unbounded right-derived unit is an isomorphism (f_*M)[0]→Rf_*(M[0]). No flatness or invertibility hypothesis is required. The map canonicalSingleDirectImageMap is constructed from that unit.

source.place: Tag 079V: unbounded direct image via K-injectives; acyclic-resolution computation (Tag 015E)

proof.text: The vanishing hypothesis makes M right-acyclic. Every term of M[0] is then right-acyclic: the degree-zero term is isomorphic to M, and the others are zero. Every term of the nonnegative injective resolution is also right-acyclic. Apply quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic to its augmentation to see that termwise pushforward preserves that quasi-isomorphism.

The nonnegative injective resolution is K-injective, so the unbounded right-derived unit there is invertible. In the unit naturality square for the augmentation, its left side is invertible by the previous step and its right side is invertible because localization inverts the augmentation. Cancel that right side to prove the unit on M[0] is invertible. Compose with the localized single-complex isomorphism.
